status_note: Reference evidence only. Nothing here is a validated runtime animation. Do not promote to imported/validated without the integration gate (docs/CROSS-PROJECT-INTEGRATION.md).
what_is_in_git: Taxonomy, registry (97 timestamped segments with phase notes), source links for all 201 clips, two raw pose JSONs, a footage-free stick-figure video, noise report, scripts.
what_is_not_in_git: The 201 video clips and 199 of the 201 pose JSONs. They are local only (E:/motion-reference/basketball/clips/<action>/) because the footage is third-party broadcast video. Regenerate from CLIP_SOURCES.json plus the tools.

units.position: pixels in the source video frame (NOT meters; contract units do not apply without a camera model)
units.time: seconds from clip start; fps stored per file (clips above 45 fps are halved)

data_format.people_per_frame: all detections, sorted by box area; track id -1 means detected but not tracked

measured_quality.method: tools/reference/noise_stats.py on all 201 clips; main player = largest box per frame
measured_quality.main_player_id_switch_rate: 0.1%-20.6% of frames by action, ~10% typical (inflated by camera cuts and the largest player changing)
measured_quality.wrist_jitter_pct_body_height_per_frame: 1.0 (steady free throw, the floor) to 6.5 (hook shot)
measured_quality.low_confidence_keypoints: 18%-54% by action; worst on catch, dribble_stationary, post_defense, celebration (occlusion)
measured_quality.slow_motion_sources: Phantom replays (~0.28x, see registry playback_speed) give pose order but NOT timing

yes: action taxonomy and phase names (anticipate/execute/contact/recover mapping)
phase timing and object-event timing (release frame, plant frame, catch) from real-speed clips, with frame-read confirmation
acceptance references: the rendered action should be compared against the linked real clip
no: driving a rig directly (2D, noisy, identity switches)
durations from slow-motion sources without the playback_speed correction

rights: Footage: third-party (YouTube standard licence, one Wikimedia Commons source). Links and timestamps only; never commit or ship clips or frames. Pose keypoints are derived measurements kept for internal research; do not ship them as game assets without review.
known_failures_to_carry_over: The U OWNERSHIP.md: four layers rewrite the shooter's arms on the jump shot (arm IK, hand_aim, elbow_hinge, arm_clearance).
torso_posture fixes some folded retargets and damages others.
Validation lesson: judge poses on the rendered mesh, never on the stick figure or joint numbers; judge motion from consecutive frames, never sampled stills.
regenerate: for each clip in CLIP_SOURCES.json: fetch the source, cut at the timestamp (tools/reference/cut_refs.py for registry segments)
